claims.text: AuCoCuNiPt nanoparticles can be investigated at atomic scale using exsolution of CoFe alloy nanoparticles.
CoFe alloy nanoparticles can be exsolved from La0.4Sr0.6Co0.2Fe0.7Mo0.1O3−δ.
An ABO3 structure is the structural mediator for the proposed investigation of AuCoCuNiPt nanoparticles.
Exsolution in the cited ABO3 system contributes to a reintegration process during catalysis.
The reintegration process during catalysis also operates in AuCoCuNiPt nanoparticles.
The proposed method produces efficient CO2 electrolysis.
The exsolution method can reveal the thermal behavior of AuCoCuNiPt nanoparticles under high-temperature application conditions.
The proposed CoFe-perovskite exsolution method is applicable within high-entropy-alloy design.
The thermal behavior measured using exsolution can be compared with results from current nanoparticle-investigation methods.

contradictions.description: The target is free-standing or otherwise unspecified AuCoCuNiPt nanoparticles, whereas the intervention concerns CoFe nanoparticle exsolution from a compositionally unrelated La–Sr–Co–Fe–Mo ABO3 oxide. No relationship connecting these material systems is stated.

The task is to investigate atomic-scale thermal behavior, but the stated outcome is efficient CO2 electrolysis rather than a measurement of thermal stability, structural evolution, or atomic-scale behavior.
